name: gtx480
description: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 480 (GF100, Fermi, sm_20) at its 700 MHz core clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 15 SMs (480 CUDA cores), 48 resident warps per SM, 2 warp schedulers per SM (NVIDIA Fermi compute architecture whitepaper; GTX 480 specifications)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: Fermi SM: 2 groups of 16 CUDA cores (FP32 and INT32), 16 LD/ST units and 4 SFUs, the cores at the 1401 MHz shader (hot) clock, twice the 700 MHz core clock (Fermi whitepaper). Each scheduler sends a warp to a 16-core group for two hot clocks, one core clock, so the profile runs at the core clock with 32 lanes per scheduler's block: the same FLOPS (15 x 2 x 32 x 2 x 700 MHz = 1344 GFLOPS) at 960 core-clock lanes against the 480 hot-clock cores, so fp32_lanes is not checked. 16 LD/ST units at the hot clock give 16 lanes per block. 700 MHz is the clock of Accel-Sim's SM2_GTX480 configuration
sources.FMA64_PE_RATIO: FP64 FMA at 1/8 of the FP32 rate on the GeForce part (the Tesla Fermi parts run it at 1/2): 32 FPU lanes / 8 = 4 F64 FMA PEs per block
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 4 SFU results per hot clock per SM, 4 per block per core clock, for the FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root on which division and square root are built: 32 / 8; 16 type conversions per hot clock per SM, 16 per block per core clock: 32 / 2 (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 2.0)
sources.NUM_TFU_LANES: 4 SFUs per SM at the hot clock: 4 results per block per core clock
sources.DCACHE_SIZE, DCACHE_NUM_WAYS: 16 KB L1 with 48 KB shared memory, the default split of the 64 KB L1/shared per SM (Fermi whitepaper): 4 ways
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE, LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 48 KB shared memory per SM; 32 banks of 4 B (16 Vortex banks of 8 B carry the same bytes per clock)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 768 KB L2 (Fermi whitepaper): 12 ways over power-of-two sets, as Accel-Sim's SM2_GTX480 (12 sub-partitions of 64 sets x 8 ways x 128 B); 16 banks with the 16 modelled channels
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 384-bit GDDR5 at 3.696 Gbps (177.4 GB/s) modelled as 16 GDDR6 x16 channels at 5544 MT/s for a power-of-two interleave: 16 x 2 B x 5.544 GT/s = 177.4 GB/s, the card's bandwidth
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE: Fermi has no tensor cores and no RT cores
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Fermi introduced a unified 64-bit virtual address space behind an MMU, global and shared-memory atomics with atomicCAS, FP16 conversion, special-function units, 16 named barriers (bar.sync 0-15, sm_20) and the graphics pipeline of a GeForce part
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.reference: dram_bandwidth_gbs is the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies: L1 hit 96, L2 hit 351 and global memory 619 cycles on the GTX 560 Ti (Mei and Chu, Dissecting GPU Memory Hierarchy through Microbenchmarking (IEEE TPDS 2017, arXiv 1509.02308), Figure 14), a GF114 with the same Fermi L1, L2 and memory pipeline. Accel-Sim correlates this card: GPGPU-Sim tested-cfg SM2_GTX480 and posted hardware runs (fermi-gtx480)
sources.L1_LINK_LATENCY: 34 core cycles each way between a core and its dcache, the L1/texture load pipeline, which the dcache bank pipeline (DCACHE_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 96-cycle L1 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 114 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py (after the L1 link) so the SimX pointer chase gives the 351-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: 210 core cycles of PHY/NoC latency beyond the links, calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX cold pointer chase gives the 619-cycle global memory latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_MSHR_SIZE: 128 per bank: Little's law on the L2-miss round trip (DRAM 619 - L2 hit 351 = 268 cycles) x 253 B/cycle (177.4 GB/s / 700 MHz) / (16 banks x 64 B) = 66.3, rounded up to a power of two. The derived default counts only PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY, which the links mostly replace
